articles.title: Steve Kerr jokes about Stephen Curry's age and compares him to Michael Jordan: "30? 29?"
articles.standfirst: The Golden State Warriors coach highlighted the point guard’s form at 38 years old and explained why watching him play reminds him of his time alongside Jordan with the Chicago Bulls.
articles.summary: The Golden State Warriors coach highlighted the point guard’s form at 38 years old and explained why watching him play reminds him of his time alongside Jordan with the Chicago Bulls.
articles.body:
Stephen Curry is 38 years old, but Steve Kerr prefers not to look at his ID when talking about his performance. The Golden State Warriors coach was asked how old he would guess the point guard to be if he did not know his age, and he replied with a laugh: "I don't know. 30? 29? He's something special".

The joke came amid the praise Kerr has devoted to his player these past few days. The coach not only highlighted his form, but also made a very special comparison: watching Curry compete at this age reminds him of what he experienced when he shared a locker room with Michael Jordan on the Chicago Bulls.

Kerr finds similarities between Curry and Michael Jordan

Kerr knows well what it means to play alongside a legend. He was part of the Chicago Bulls during Jordan's second stint with the team and now, after more than a decade at the helm of the Warriors, he finds similar traits in Curry. He is not referring only to talent, but to the ability to keep making a difference even though defenses prepare specific strategies to stop them.

"Honestly, it reminds me so much of what it was like playing with Michael Jordan back then," the coach explained. He also noted that, night after night, it is surprising what Curry can do, regardless of the methods his rivals use to stop him.

Curry's secret to staying among the best

In another interview, this time on the Tom Tolbert Show, Kerr went deeper into the reasons that explain the point guard's longevity. For the coach, his performance is not the result of chance. Behind his ability to keep competing at the highest level is a constant commitment to physical preparation and endurance .

"I think it is very unusual to see someone like that. Players who can sustain it for that long usually share the same qualities in terms of total commitment to their physical preparation and their endurance," Kerr commented. In that group he also mentioned John Stockton, Steve Nash, and LeBron James, players who managed to maintain a very high competitive level during the final part of their careers.

The coach also focused on Curry's passion for basketball. His competitiveness and his desire to put on a show remain aspects that, in his view, are reminiscent of Jordan.

At 38 years old, Curry is playing his eighteenth NBA season and remains one of Golden State’s main offensive references. His coach’s praise carries added value: Kerr closely experienced Jordan’s time in Chicago and now watches from the bench as the Warriors point guard continues to deliver top-level performances

articles.title: Philadelphia 76ers vs Chicago Bulls: Where to watch Sunday's game and what time is the first pitch
articles.standfirst: The Bulls, at the bottom of the East, host the unstoppable 76ers at the United Center
articles.summary: The Bulls, at the bottom of the East, host the unstoppable 76ers at the United Center
articles.body:
Few stories better encapsulate the current divide in the Eastern Conference than the one that will unfold this Sunday at the United Center . In one corner, the Chicago Bulls , languishing at the bottom of their conference; in the other, the Philadelphia 76ers, currently tied for first place in the entire NBA.

The clash promises to be a reality test for the home team and a golden opportunity for the visitors to further solidify their credentials as contenders.

When and where to watch 76ers vs Bulls?

The game between the Chicago Bulls and the Philadelphia 76ers will be played on Sunday, November 8, 2026, with tip-off at 3:30 p.m. (2:30 p.m. Central Time and 12:30 p.m. Pacific Time). The game will be held at the United Center in Chicago, which has a capacity of 20,917 fans.

You can watch this game streamed on NBA League Pass, as well as on various local channels in Philadelphia and Chicago.

NBA Standings overview: how Chicago and Philadelphia are approaching today's game

The difference in context couldn't be more stark. Philadelphia comes in sitting atop the Eastern Conference with an 8-2 record, sharing first place overall in the league with the Los Angeles Lakers. The Sixers also lead the Atlantic Division, half a game ahead of the Boston Celtics.

Chicago, on the other hand, is having a forgettable start to the season. The Bulls are second to last in the East with just 1 win and 7 losses, placing them third to last in the entire NBA.

They are currently fourth in the Central Division, five games behind the division-leading Detroit Pistons. The most worrying statistic for home fans is their defense: having allowed 1,037 points in eight games and with a -144 point differential, Chicago has the worst scoring gap in the East.

Sixers vs Chicago lineups: experience versus rebuild

Philadelphia boasts a roster that blends explosive youth with a veteran heavyweight. Shooting guard Tyrese Maxey anchors the backcourt, supported by Jaylen Brown on the perimeter and Joel Embiid's presence in the paint.

Joining this core is 41-year-old LeBron James, who brings leadership and ball-handling skills, along with shooters like Kentavious Caldwell-Pope and Anfernee Simons. Young prospect VJ Edgecombe, just 21, rounds out a rotation with both established talent and future potential.

On the other side, the Bulls are betting on a much more inexperienced project. Australian Josh Giddey directs the offense from point guard, with scoring support from Norman Powell and Buddy Hield from beyond the arc.

The front row features young names like Lithuanian Matas Buzelis and Frenchman Noa Essengue, both just 19 years old, while Nic Claxton and Zach Collins share minutes in the post. It's a rotation with promising potential, but the early start has taken its toll.

Fight for the lead and danger zone

For Philadelphia, every win carries double the weight in the tightly contested top of the league: with the Lakers, Celtics, Rockets, Thunder, and Spurs breathing down their necks, the Sixers can't afford to slip up against rivals they're expected to beat. Maintaining their lead in the East and the Atlantic Division requires winning precisely these kinds of games.

Chicago, meanwhile, is already eyeing the bottom of the standings. Only the Milwaukee Bucks are below them in the East, and in the overall standings they share last place with the Clippers, Bucks, Kings, and Jazz. Reversing this trend is urgent before the season slips away from them in November.

What is the prediction for the Philadelphia 76ers vs Chicago Bulls game?

The context is stark: Philadelphia arrives as co-leaders of the NBA, while Chicago is one of the worst teams in the league, with a devastating point differential. At home, the Bulls can rely on the energy of their fans and the scoring prowess of Powell and Hield to make the game competitive at times, but the visitors' experience, depth, and solidity make the difference.

Everything points to a 76ers victory, who must continue to add points to defend their lead in the East.

articles.title: LA Lakers vs Detroit Pistons: Where to watch Luka Doncic today and what time the game starts at Little Caesars Arena
articles.standfirst: Pistons and Lakers, showdown of leaders in Detroit: Cunningham hosts a Luka who just keeps winning
articles.summary: Pistons and Lakers, showdown of leaders in Detroit: Cunningham hosts a Luka who just keeps winning
articles.body:
The NBA schedule delivers one of those matchups that mean more than just a regular-season game. The Detroit Pistons , who have become the big surprise in the East, host the Lakers , who lead the West.

Two trains launched at full speed cross paths in the Motor City, and here we tell you all the details of the game.

Where to watch and what time do the Lakers vs. Pistons play?

The game between Detroit and Los Angeles will take place this Sunday, November 8, at 6:00 p.m. Eastern Time (5:00 p.m. Central Time and 3:00 p.m. Pacific Time) , at the Little Caesars Arena in Detroit will open its doors, a venue with a capacity of 20,491 fans.

Nationwide, the broadcast will be carried by NBA TV, with local coverage on Spectrum SportsNet, Bally Sports Detroit, and FanDuel Sports Network; while you can stream it on: Fubo, YouTube TV, DIRECTV, Sling TV, and with NBA League Pass.

Preview: Lakers vs. Pistons standings and recent results

The standings photo says it all. The Lakers rule the Western Conference and share first place in the entire NBA with a record of 8 wins and 2 losses (80% wins), identical to that of the Philadelphia 76ers.

The Pistons, meanwhile, lead the Central Division comfortably and sit in third place in the East, just one game behind the top spot held by the Sixers and the Boston Celtics.

What stands out most is the Angels' offensive firepower: the Lakers have scored 1,220 points, the highest total in the entire league, with a +77 point differential.

Detroit, by contrast, builds its success on solidity: it has allowed only 814 points in 8 games, the best defensive mark among the leading teams, for a +75 differential that speaks to a very balanced squad.

The Lakers come in hot. In their last eight games they have only lost once, a thrilling 129-136 against Portland. Since then they have put together a devastating run to close out: 103-87 against the Clippers, 131-125 against Toronto, a commanding 138-117 over Miami and, in their most recent visit, 116-103 in Sacramento. This is a team that scores in bunches and has also learned to win through control.

The Pistons are not far behind, although their path has been bumpier. They opened the season by knocking off the Celtics and strung together some significant wins, including a 106-93 victory in Philadelphia. Their most recent steamrolling was a crushing 124-91 over Charlotte, but they are coming off a 106-112 home loss to the 76ers. They will want to wash away that defeat in front of their fans and against a high-profile opponent.

The stellar duel: Cunningham vs. Dončić

The biggest attraction is at point guard. 25-year-old Cade Cunningham, wearing number 2, is the engine of these Pistons : the American carries on his shoulders the playmaking duties of a team that has made defense its calling card.

Around him, Detroit has young pieces with enormous potential such as center Jalen Duren and versatile forward Ausar Thompson, as well as reliable shooters like Duncan Robinson and Kevin Huerter.

On the other side appears Luka Dončić, the 27-year-old Slovenian wearing number 77, a true beacon of an offense that overwhelms whoever stands in its way. He is joined by a luxury backcourt featuring Austin Reaves and Collin Sexton, while the paint is left under the responsibility of Walker Kessler and the veteran Kevon Looney.

The tactical question is served up: the Lakers' top-tier offense against the best defense among the Eastern contenders.

What's at stake at the top of the NBA standings

For the Lakers, every victory is pure gold in a brutally tight Western Conference: Houston, Oklahoma City and San Antonio are all sitting at 7-2 and breathing down their necks. Losing their footing in Detroit could cost them first place in the West and in the league.

For the Pistons, beating the NBA leaders would be a statement of intent. T hey are just one game away from the top of the East, and a win of this magnitude would place them firmly in the conversation among the conference’s top contenders, ahead of Cleveland (14th overall) in their own division and closing in on the Celtics and Sixers.

Lakers vs Pistons Prediction: Which team is favored to win?

The league’s best offense and one of its most reliable defenses collide. The Lakers arrive in overwhelming form and with greater scoring depth, but Detroit is playing at home, defends like few others, and has wounded pride after the loss to Philadelphia.

I expect a back-and-forth game, the kind that gets decided in the final quarter. Dončić's firepower tips the scales slightly toward the Angelenos, although it wouldn't surprise me at all if the atmosphere at Little Caesars Arena pushes the Pistons to pull off the upset. Slight favorites: the Lakers, but with home-court advantage as the great equalizer.
